trips.name: Sigurtà gardens and Borghetto mills
trips.why_selected: Famous-lake lists skip inland Valeggio. You should not. This is the highest-scoring day in the menu: easy parking, a stroller-native garden, and a lunch with a name. You are not here to collect a castle queue. You are here because a six-month-old and a good plate of tortellini can share the same morning.
trips.short: A shaded garden built for slow walking, then a mill-race postcard, then the tortellini this family will talk about at dinner. Inland, unhurried, home for the nap.

transport.mode_summary: Car the whole way. Bardolino → Peschiera corridor → Valeggio sul Mincio.
transport.route: SR249 south through Cisano and Lazise, then inland signed Valeggio / Parco Sigurtà. Do not detour via Gardaland.
transport.parking_location: Sigurtà park lots Rosso and Giallo on arrival. After the garden, signed Borghetto / Valeggio lots (Via Cavour / Italmark area).
transport.parking_cost: Park lots typically free/unattended. Village lots cheap or free. Budget €0–5.
transport.parking_difficulty: Easy — the parking win of the holiday.
transport.notes: Buy Sigurtà tickets online in tulip/high season. Ages 0–4 usually free — verify sigurta.it.
transport.maps_lot: Parco Giardino Sigurtà — Rosso / Giallo lots
transport.maps_address: Via Cavour, 1, 37067 Valeggio sul Mincio VR
transport.parking_backup: Italmark / Via Cavour lots in Valeggio if the village edge is busy.
transport.ztl: No Bardolino-style ZTL trap here. Do not follow GPS into Borghetto mill lanes; they are not a car park.

experience.walking_route: Forty-five to sixty minutes easy on porphyry avenues, plus a short mill-village amble. Cap it. The park will happily sell you a 10 km day you do not want.
experience.walking_duration: 45–60 minutes easy, plus optional train rest
experience.stroller_friendliness: Yes on park avenues. Carrier for Borghetto’s last steps. The park does not rent strollers.
viewpoints: Viale delle rose toward Valeggio’s Scaliger castle
restaurants: Tortellini di Valeggio in brodo or burro e salvia
Park cafe only as a snack
hidden_gems: Mill race light if you still leave by 15:40
experience.skip: The full garden circuit, golf-cart FOMO, and driving into mill lanes for a closer photo.
experience.place_food: Tortellini di Valeggio is the lunch to spend on. The park cafe is a snack, not the point.
experience.place_coffee: A Valeggio bar after the village photos. Not a third course.
experience.place_gem: The mill race at Borghetto in late light — only if you still leave by 15:40.

family.baby_changing: Accessible toilets on the Sigurtà main circuit. Change on arrival so Borghetto is not a hunt.
family.places_to_rest: Shaded benches, lawns, panoramic train, restaurant nap in the carrier.
family.stroller_notes: Stroller primary in the park. Carrier for Borghetto’s last photogenic steps and cobbles.
crowded_areas_to_avoid: Tulip-season weekend gates at opening selfie hour; Borghetto bridge at Saturday 13:00. Check Monday restaurant closures.

costs.food_estimate: €40–70 (this is the lunch to spend on)
costs.tickets: Sigurtà adult ~€18; 0–4 usually free; train extra if used

backup.rainy_day_alternative: Keep Valeggio lunch — that is the food score. Skip wet lawns. Add Museo del Vino Zeni back in Bardolino after. Do not ‘save the day’ with Sirmione; the ZTL does not get kinder in rain.

timeline.title: Drive inland
timeline.detail: Take the lake road south, then follow signs for Valeggio / Sigurtà. Ignore any Gardaland signs.

timeline.title: Park at Sigurtà
timeline.detail: Use the Rosso or Giallo car park. Get the stroller out and put hats on.

timeline.title: Short garden walk
timeline.detail: Stay in the shade. See the rose avenue viewpoint and sit on a lawn. Do not try to cover every path.

timeline.title: Optional park train
timeline.detail: Only if someone is tired. Treat it as a rest, not another attraction.

timeline.title: Borghetto mills
timeline.detail: Five-minute drive. Park in the signed village lots — never on the narrow mill lanes. Walk 20–30 minutes.

timeline.title: Tortellini lunch in Valeggio
timeline.detail: Order tortellini in broth or with butter and sage. Sit down properly. This is the highlight of the day.

timeline.title: Drive home
timeline.detail: The lake road may be busier, but you still have time. Back at the apartment by about 16:20.

trips.rationale: Named lots, shade, toilets, and a panoramic train if anyone folds — parking and baby both near the top of the scale. Beauty is river-and-garden rather than a famous castle, which is the point of the ranking.

trips.name: Bardolino wine and olive oil morning
trips.why_selected: Six days is too many away days. This is how a Garda specialist sells a rest morning without calling it a wasted day: Zeni’s wine museum, the olive strip toward Cisano, a proper lunch one street inland, and a nap in a real cot. You still live on the lake at 17:30.
trips.short: The rest-day product: a cantina museum, an olive mill, lunch inland of the pier, and the apartment for the nap. No trophy town. No SR249 project.

transport.mode_summary: Walk from the apartment, or a 4-minute drive to Zeni’s visitor bays.
transport.route: Via Costabella for Zeni. Olive museum / shore toward Cisano on the lungolago.
transport.parking_location: Cantina Zeni visitor parking at Via Costabella 9. Otherwise the apartment.
transport.parking_difficulty: Easy.
transport.notes: Confirm Zeni opening hours the night before. Mondays can be quiet.
transport.maps_lot: Cantina Zeni / Museo del Vino visitor parking
transport.maps_address: Via Costabella, 9, 37011 Bardolino VR
transport.parking_backup: Bardolino centro paid lots if Zeni’s small bays are full — then walk.
transport.ztl: Stay out of the tiny one-way harbour cuts. You do not need them.

experience.walking_route: Twenty to forty minutes total, all stroller, broken by indoor rooms.
experience.stroller_friendliness: Yes. Best stroller morning of the week after Cisano beach.
viewpoints: Bardolino rooftops from the cantina terrace if you step out
restaurants: Inland Bardolino trattoria
Apartment kitchen
coffee_stops: Via Goffredo Mameli bar with indoor chairs
hidden_gems: Olive strip when the harbour is loud
experience.skip: A ‘since we’re up, let’s add Lazise’ add-on. That turns a rest day into a trip.
experience.place_food: Inland trattoria or the apartment kitchen. This is not a tasting-menu day.
experience.place_coffee: Any bar on Via Goffredo Mameli — indoor chairs, not the waterfront selfie rail.
experience.place_gem: The olive trees between Bardolino and Cisano when the harbour is loud.

family.baby_changing: Go home. That is the luxury of a base-town morning.
family.places_to_rest: Museum chairs, then the cot. Do not negotiate a harbour bench nap.
family.stroller_notes: Stroller is fine. Carrier only if the baby is already asleep on you.
crowded_areas_to_avoid: Harbour at 11:00 in August. You are inland on purpose.

backup.rainy_day_alternative: This is already the rain-friendly rest day. Stay inside Zeni, skip the olive walk, go home. Do not invent a Verona dash because you feel idle.

timeline.title: Slow breakfast at the apartment
timeline.detail: No early rush. Still pack the baby carrier.

timeline.title: Wine museum at Cantina Zeni
timeline.detail: A short indoor visit. Taste a little wine, or skip the glass if you are driving the short way home.

timeline.title: Olive shore / oil museum if open
timeline.detail: Walk the lakeside path toward Cisano. Stroller-friendly, shady, no hike.

timeline.title: Lunch inland in Bardolino
timeline.detail: Avoid the touristy waterfront menus. Choose a place one street back from the pier.

timeline.title: Home for the baby’s nap
timeline.detail: That nap is the point of this easy day. Save gelato for after 17:00.

trips.rationale: Parking is the apartment or a named cantina lot; baby score is near-max because you can go home between stops. Beauty is local hillside, not a postcard castle — honest, and still a better morning than a forced city.

trips.name: East-shore ferry: Garda and Torri
trips.why_selected: You asked for a Garda boat day. The specialist version is Bardolino → Garda → Torri on Navigazione Laghi passenger boats, then home. The slow boat to Riva is how families miss 18:00. You will not do that. Wind can cancel; that is a land day, not a stubbornness test.
trips.short: The lake from the water, car at the apartment, Torri’s courtyard as the cultural bite. A half-to-three-quarter day — not a slow boat to Riva.

transport.mode_summary: Walk or 4-minute drive to Bardolino imbarcadero. Passenger boats only. Car stays home.
transport.route: Apartment to the ferry landing. No SR249.
transport.parking_location: Apartment. If you drive the last 400 m, signed imbarcadero / lungolago paid bays.
transport.parking_cost: €0 if you walk; otherwise a few euros local rate. Budget €0–8.
transport.parking_difficulty: Easy — the easiest parking day of the holiday.
transport.notes: Buy tickets early. Check Navigazione Laghi the night before. Infant fares: verify current policy.
transport.maps_lot: Apartment first; else Imbarcadero / lungolago bays
transport.maps_address: Piazzale Nazioni Unite / Imbarcadero, 37011 Bardolino VR
transport.parking_backup: Bardolino centro paid lots a few minutes’ walk. Wind can cancel boats: decide by 09:00.
transport.ztl: None that matters. Do not block the landing ‘for a minute’.

experience.walking_route: Thirty to forty minutes on land. Castle interior stairs optional and skippable.
experience.stroller_friendliness: Mixed. Fold for gangways; carrier during boarding and if there is swell.
viewpoints: Deck view back to the olive hills
beaches: Look, don’t commit. Pebbly edges at Garda. Baia delle Sirene is a different product.
restaurants: Torri: one street off the first pier
Garda: pastry, not a second lunch
hidden_gems: Optional Torri↔Maderno hop only if ahead of timetable
experience.skip: Riva, Malcesine, the Maderno car traghetto ‘for fun’, and a Baia delle Sirene detour unless the baby is angelic and the timetable agrees.
experience.place_food: Torri trattoria inland of the first row. Garda is coffee, not a second lunch.
experience.place_coffee: Garda waterfront bar with shade; Bardolino gelato on return — you are already home.
experience.place_gem: Foot-passenger Torri↔Maderno only if you are ahead of timetable. Never chase it.

family.baby_changing: Bardolino cafe before boarding; Torri cafe on arrival. Not the boat WC.
family.places_to_rest: Indoor cabin seats, Torri piazzetta, Garda benches.
family.stroller_notes: Fold the stroller for gangways. One adult boards first with the carrier. Never block the ramp.
crowded_areas_to_avoid: First-and-last August boats; the noisy vehicle deck of the Maderno traghetto.

costs.ferry: ~€25–45 for two adults return plus Garda hop; check infant fare

backup.rainy_day_alternative: If boats cancel or the deck is a wind tunnel: do not start a long cruise because you imagined a boat. Swap to Zeni, Peschiera cafes, or Torri by car in light rain only.

timeline.title: Change the baby at home
timeline.detail: Boat toilets are a bad place for a nappy change.

timeline.title: Bardolino ferry pier
timeline.detail: Buy or collect tickets about 20 minutes early. Check yesterday’s timetable on navigazionelaghi.it.

timeline.title: Boat toward Garda / Torri
timeline.detail: Confirm the exact sailing time. Sit inside the cabin if the open deck feels windy or rough.

timeline.title: Short stop in Garda town
timeline.detail: Coffee, shade, a few photos. Do not linger — this is not the beach day at Punta San Vigilio.

timeline.title: Arrive Torri del Benaco
timeline.detail: See the castle courtyard and harbour. Skip the museum stairs with the baby.

timeline.title: Lunch in Torri
timeline.detail: Eat one street back from the pier if the waterfront menus look touristy.

timeline.title: Return boat
timeline.detail: Leave earlier if clouds build up. Back at the apartment around 16:10.

trips.rationale: Parking is almost a perfect score because the car stays home. Baby is 80, not 95: gangways, sun, and possible swell are real, and a carrier plus a short timetable is the fix — not a longer cruise.

trips.name: Cavaion and the Bardolino Classico road
trips.why_selected: The Classico hills behind Bardolino are a morning, not a wine-tour odyssey. Cavaion Veronese sits on SP31 with estates that expect cars. You park at a named cantina, you do one visit, you eat, you come home. Two estates is greed with a newborn.
trips.short: Fifteen minutes inland to visitor-ready cantinas, shade, and a tasting you can skip if you are driving. The baby sleeps in the carrier while you look at barrels.

transport.mode_summary: Car inland. Bardolino → Calmasino → Cavaion Veronese.
transport.route: Leave the lake road early. SP31 toward Cavaion / Affi. Do not add San Zeno di Montagna ‘for the view’ — that is a different, hillier product we are not selling.
transport.parking_location: The estate’s own signed visitor parking. Gravel is normal. Do not park on SP31 verges.
transport.parking_cost: Usually free at the cantina. Budget €0–3.
transport.parking_difficulty: Easy if you pick one estate with a visible P. Hard if you hunt cellar doors without signs.
transport.notes: Email or call one cantina the night before. Walk-ins work on quiet weekdays; Saturdays want a booking. Driver drinks water.
transport.maps_lot: Signed visitor parking at a Cavaion / Costermano-road cantina
transport.maps_address: Cavaion Veronese VR — SP31 / Via Provincia cantina lots (pick one estate, park on their signed gravel)
transport.parking_backup: Cavaion village square / church-adjacent bays, then walk. Affi supermarket if you abort.
transport.ztl: None. Rural roads, not cameras.

experience.walking_route: Ten to twenty minutes around the courtyard and village. This is not a vineyard hike.
experience.stroller_friendliness: Yes on courtyards. Carrier in wet cellars.
viewpoints: First terrace behind Cavaion toward the lake — from the lot, not a hike
restaurants: Cavaion or Calmasino trattoria
Cheese plate at the cantina if lunch is late
hidden_gems: Lake glimpse from the cantina car park
experience.skip: A three-cantina crawl, San Zeno viewpoint, and ‘we’re halfway to Valpolicella so let’s keep going’.
experience.place_food: Inland trattoria in Cavaion or Calmasino. Better value than Bardolino harbour.
experience.place_coffee: Bar in Cavaion centro. Indoor, quick.
experience.place_gem: The view back to the lake from the first terrace behind Cavaion — from the car park, not a trail.

family.baby_changing: Ask at the cantina; most have a WC. Otherwise the village bar.
family.places_to_rest: Cellar rooms are cool. Carrier nap during the talk is normal and welcome.
family.stroller_notes: Stroller on gravel courtyards is fine. Carrier inside the cellar if floors are wet.
crowded_areas_to_avoid: Weekend bus tastings. Weekday late morning is civilised.

costs.tickets: Tasting often €10–20, waived with a bottle; infant free

backup.rainy_day_alternative: Cellars love rain. Keep the booking, skip any terrace, go home after lunch. Strong rest-day swap for Sigurtà.

timeline.title: Drive inland to Cavaion
timeline.detail: Go via Calmasino / Cavaion, not along the lake. Bring a cool bag, hats, and one planned winery.

timeline.title: Park at the winery
timeline.detail: Use the signed visitor parking. Take a quick photo of where you parked so you can find the car later.

timeline.title: One cellar visit
timeline.detail: Keep it under 50 minutes. If you are driving, spit tastings or skip alcohol.

timeline.title: Pause in Cavaion village
timeline.detail: Coffee, shade, and a nappy change. Do not add a second tasting.

timeline.title: Lunch inland
timeline.detail: Simple food — risotto, grilled vegetables, or a cheese plate.

timeline.title: Drive home
timeline.detail: Apartment by about 14:50 for the afternoon nap.

trips.rationale: Cantina visitor lots are the parking story — short, signed, usually empty compared with harbour towns. Baby score is high because this is indoor, air-conditioned, and close enough to abort. Food is the second priority after beaches, and this is how you honour it without a city.

trips.name: Cisano and Bardolino beaches
trips.why_selected: Beaches are priority one. The apartment is on the east shore. A Garda specialist does not send you to Sirmione for a swim you can take at Cisano before lunch. Use two of six days here so the away days do not wreck the baby.
trips.short: Home shore, pebble lidos, shade, and gelato after the nap. Two of the six days belong here on purpose — beaches are the first priority, and you already live on the right bank.

transport.mode_summary: Walk from the apartment. Drive only if you want Cisano’s slightly quieter strip.
transport.route: Lungolago south toward Cisano, or the apartment door to Bardolino lido.
transport.parking_location: Apartment. If you drive to Cisano: small paid lungolago bays, not the curve of SR249.
transport.parking_difficulty: Easy.
transport.notes: Bring your own shade. Lido umbrellas are optional euros, not a requirement.
transport.maps_lot: Walk from the apartment; else Cisano lungolago paid bays
transport.maps_address: Lungolago / Via Gardesana, Cisano di Bardolino VR
transport.parking_backup: Walk back to Bardolino lots. Always abort toward home, never toward Lazise.
transport.ztl: None that matters.

viewpoints: Olive shore toward the west-side mountains
restaurants: Inland Bardolino
Apartment kitchen
hidden_gems: Olive strip when the harbour is loud

experience.place_coffee: Any inland bar. Sit inside if the promenade is a fry pan.
experience.place_gem: Museo dell’Olio / olive strip when the harbour is loud.

family.baby_changing: Go home. That is the luxury.
family.places_to_rest: Shade, then the cot. Do not let the baby sleep only in the stroller all afternoon.
family.stroller_notes: Stroller primary. Carrier at the waterline on pebbles.
crowded_areas_to_avoid: Saturday 16:00 lungolago. You will already be napping.

timeline.detail: No early rush.

timeline.title: Cisano or Bardolino lakeside
timeline.detail: Stroller, shade tent, feet in the water. Expect pebbles or concrete, not soft sand.

timeline.title: Lunch inland in Bardolino
timeline.detail: Skip the touristy pier restaurants.

timeline.title: Home for the nap
timeline.detail: That rest is the point of this base day.

timeline.title: Harbour gelato
timeline.detail: Only after you are already home. Dinner stays in Bardolino.

trips.rationale: Baby and walking nearly max out because the cot is ten minutes away. Beauty is honest east-shore olive, not Punta. Effort is almost perfect: this is not a trip, and that is why it scores like a gift.

trips.name: Castellaro Lagusello
trips.why_selected: Castellaro is Borghetto’s shy cousin: a castle, a lagoon, almost no coach parking. It is not a Sigurtà duplicate. It is the morning you pick when you want walls and water without mill-lane chaos. If you already did Borghetto this week, skip this — same inland direction, diminishing returns.
trips.short: A tiny walled village on its own lagoon — quieter than Borghetto’s selfie hour, with one lot and one slow loop. Do this or Sigurtà, not both in the same breathless weekend.

transport.mode_summary: Car inland. Bardolino → Peschiera corridor → Monzambano → Castellaro Lagusello.
transport.route: Same first half as Sigurtà, then continue toward Monzambano. Follow Castellaro signs, not Borghetto.
transport.parking_location: Parcheggio at the village edge on Via Castello. Small, usually sufficient before 11:00.
transport.parking_cost: Often free or a low hourly. Budget €0–5.
transport.parking_difficulty: Easy in the morning. Awkward if you arrive at Saturday lunch.
transport.notes: This is a 90-minute visit plus lunch. It is not a half-day hike around the lagoon.
transport.maps_lot: Parcheggio Castellaro Lagusello (village edge)
transport.maps_address: Via Castello / village car park, 46040 Castellaro Lagusello, Monzambano MN
transport.parking_backup: Monzambano centro lots and skip Castellaro if the lane is blocked — rare, but aborting is allowed.
transport.ztl: The historic kernel is not for cars. Park outside and walk. No Sirmione-scale cameras, still no squeezing.

experience.walking_route: Thirty to forty-five minutes on cobbles and a flat lagoon path. Cap it. No circuit of the whole water.
experience.stroller_friendliness: Mixed cobbles. Carrier-primary.
restaurants: Village trattoria if open
Valeggio tortellini as backup
hidden_gems: Far-corner lagoon bench away from the first viewpoint
experience.skip: Combining with Sigurtà/Borghetto the same day. Combining with Mantua ‘since we’re south’.
experience.place_food: One village trattoria if open; otherwise drive 10 minutes to Valeggio and do tortellini without the garden.
experience.place_coffee: The bar on the tiny piazza. If it is closed, you are on a short-visit day — that is fine.
experience.place_gem: The lagoon from the walls at the far quiet corner, away from the first viewpoint bench.

family.baby_changing: Bar WC if open; otherwise a nappy in the car before the loop.
family.places_to_rest: Shaded wall bench, then the car. No museum interiors required.
family.stroller_notes: Carrier-primary on cobbles. Compact stroller only if the cobbles are dry and you are patient.
crowded_areas_to_avoid: Weekend wedding photography. Weekdays feel private.

costs.tickets: €0 unless a small castle opening exists — skip interiors

backup.rainy_day_alternative: A wet cobble village with one bar is a thin morning. Swap to Valeggio lunch + Zeni, or keep Cavaion’s cellar.

timeline.title: Drive inland past Peschiera
timeline.detail: Head toward Monzambano / Castellaro. Stay inland — this is not a lakeside stop.

timeline.title: Park at the village edge
timeline.detail: Use the signed car park outside the walls. Walk in. Do not try to drive through the gate.

timeline.title: Walls and little lake loop
timeline.detail: 30–40 minutes. Use the carrier on cobbles. One viewpoint, then sit.

timeline.title: Lunch if the trattoria is open
timeline.detail: Many places close on Monday. Keep Valeggio as a backup lunch stop.

timeline.title: Drive home
timeline.detail: Apartment by about 15:40. Do not add Borghetto ‘because it is close’.

trips.rationale: A village car park with a short walk beats every harbour scramble. Baby is high because the loop is small and the streets empty out. Food is a notch below Valeggio — one trattoria, not a destination cuisine — and the score says so.

trips.name: Peschiera fortress and lido
trips.why_selected: You live in a harbour town already. Peschiera is the away-day that still honours the beach brief: star-fort canals, a lido, gelato, and Parcheggio Fortezza. It beat Lazise because it feels like a destination. It beat Sirmione because you will actually find a space. Do not combine it with the Venice morning.
trips.short: The rare Garda town that gives you a swim, shade, toilets, gelato, and a named lot that is not a peninsula trap. Fortress walls, then feet in the water, then home for the nap.

transport.mode_summary: Car SR249 south. Park at the fortress lots. Walk the walls. Swim. Drive home.
transport.route: Bardolino → Cisano → Lazise → Peschiera. Stay on the lake road unless jammed, then inland via Calmasino.
transport.parking_location: Parcheggio Fortezza / signed wall-side lots. Not the historic-centre door.
transport.parking_cost: Typical Garda hourly. Plan €6–12 for the stay.
transport.parking_difficulty: Moderate at ~09:30. Hard after 11:30 in August.
transport.notes: Skip every Gardaland sign. Nearest east-shore ER pointer is also here (Pederzoli) — know it, do not tour it.
transport.maps_lot: Parcheggio Fortezza / signed wall-side lots
transport.maps_address: Viale della Fortezza / wall-side parking, 37019 Peschiera del Garda VR
transport.parking_backup: Station-area overflow (Piazzale Stazione) and walk. Different use from the Venice day — do not stack them.
transport.ztl: Not Sirmione, but do not follow GPS through pedestrian cuts on the fortress.

experience.walking_route: Thirty-five to forty-five minutes plus a beach sit.
experience.stroller_friendliness: Yes on the main fortress circuit. Carrier for stepped bastions.
viewpoints: Canal cuts through the star fort
beaches: Family lidos on the Peschiera waterfront — pebble/concrete, not fine sand
restaurants: Simple lunch near Porta Verona / walls
Gelato as dessert
coffee_stops: Cafe on the walls with water both sides
hidden_gems: Quieter wall stretches away from the bus-tour pause

experience.place_food: Simple lunch, gelato as dessert.
experience.place_coffee: Wall cafe with water both sides.
experience.place_gem: Quieter wall stretches away from the bus-tour pause.

family.baby_changing: Lido changing rooms in season; otherwise a cafe WC before the beach sit.
family.places_to_rest: Shade trees on the walls, lido umbrellas, cafe interiors.
family.stroller_notes: Stroller primary on the fortress circuit. Carrier for any stepped bastion and the car.
crowded_areas_to_avoid: Harbor bus-photo corner at noon; Gardaland-bound traffic on the ring.

costs.tickets: Fortress exterior is a walk. Lido sunbed optional €10–20

backup.rainy_day_alternative: Keep Peschiera for cafes and arcades, skip the lido. Or swap the calendar day with Venice if the forecast is a single-day washout. If both are wet: Zeni + apartment.

timeline.title: Drive south on the lake road
timeline.detail: Leave before traffic builds. If maps show a jam, go inland via Calmasino.

timeline.title: Park at Fortezza car park
timeline.detail: Get the stroller out and hats on. Do not try to park at a historic-centre doorway.

timeline.title: Walk the walls and canals
timeline.detail: A slow loop. Watch for bikes.

timeline.title: Coffee break
timeline.detail: Feed the baby in the shade. Choose a wall café with water views if you can.

timeline.title: Short lunch
timeline.detail: Near Porta Verona. Not a long tasting-menu meal.

timeline.title: Beach / lido sit
timeline.detail: Feet in the water under a shade tent. Not a swimming lesson.

timeline.title: Drive home
timeline.detail: Leave before the late-afternoon lake road gets bad. Apartment around 15:50. Save gelato for Bardolino later.

trips.rationale: Beaches are priority one; this is the easiest proper swim-and-stroll that still feels like going somewhere. Beauty is military-picturesque, scored 78 on purpose. Parking is not Sirmione, and that 20% weight is why this beats the famous castle.

trips.name: Soave castle town
trips.why_selected: Soave is what people think Sirmione will feel like: a castle, a wall, wine, and a piazza — except you can park. It is east of Verona, about 45 minutes, and it is a town you can read in two hours. Skip the steep keep with the stroller; the streets are the visit.
trips.short: A real castle town with wine in the streets, parking outside the walls, and a 45-minute drive that still gets you home by tea. Easy, readable, baby-tolerant if you skip the keep.

transport.mode_summary: Car east. Bardolino → Affi/A22 or A4 toward Soave. Park outside the walls.
transport.route: Do not pin ‘Castello di Soave’ as a driving destination — that GPS wants the hill. Pin a signed parcheggio at the foot.
transport.parking_location: Parcheggio Castello / Piazzale della Vittoria / wall-outside signed lots.
transport.parking_difficulty: Easy in the morning. Moderate Saturday lunch.
transport.notes: Castle keep is a climb. The product is the town, not the ramparts with a newborn.
transport.maps_lot: Parcheggio Castello / signed lots outside the walls
transport.maps_address: Via Castello / Piazzale della Vittoria lots, 37038 Soave VR

Coach tours steal nap control and often return after 18:00. Winner: twenty minutes to Peschiera station, a direct train to Venezia Santa Lucia (~1h28). You arrive in Venice, not in a garage. Then you do a small day and you leave.
